quest.title: Beneath the Crystal Rock
quest.description: Help Titu resolve the Shadow Pin issue and reinforce the seal placed upon the Abyss.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.text: ...This is a big problem. Man, haha, what terrible luck! Still, wouldn't this make for a pretty interesting story opener?

"Titu, the tribe's old storyteller, spoke of what he had seen: On the day of that great earthquake, he saw the giant Shadow Pin plunge beneath the earth — and that was how all the calamities began..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa. This person sure is spouting some scary stuff.
Ah, yes. "You've sure gotten slow. Didn't even notice them until they were right under your nose." That line's from a story I read recently. Made a real impression on me.
Still, if you ask me, eavesdropping isn't usually considered a sign of virtue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't blame us, you were the one talking super loudly.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!
Really? Well, that makes things awkward... And hey! C'mon, little fella, why are you backing these outlanders? Just whose side are you on?

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr... Rawrr!
Alright, alright... Still, it's quite the strange little ensemble. Two outlanders and a special little Tepetlisaurus. That social studies bookworm sure would love to see this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wait, you can understand what {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}'s saying?
#Understand Saurian-speak? Haha, you've got to be kidding me. No one can do that! What do you think they'd say anyway? "Hello, my name is {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}"?

But I'm one of the Children of Echoes, and we're always around Tepetlisaurs. You can figure out what they're trying to communicate from their eyes, their expressions, and the humming noises they make.
Anyway, introductions are in order. Titu... That's my name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #And this is {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Since we've introduced ourselves without a fight, that makes us friends... and word of advice from a friend — this place is dangerous. Why don't you head over to the People of the Springs instead?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: They've got it all over there: hot springs, relaxing music, chicks and hunks in swimsuits, the works. All we've got here is a couple of huge stone pillars. It even sounds boring...

choices.text: Whoa, now those are big stone pillars!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Uh, that's... not the response I expected. In fact, that's a worrying amount of excitement about... *sigh* big stone pillars...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: It's been doing poorly of late, I'm afraid. "The Shadow Pin's spirit was weakening, and the shadow it should have pinned in place would soon silently slip away..."

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Hmm. You know what? That would make a good starting point for a story.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Ehrrr?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah, sorry, got a bit carried away thinking about stories there. Telling{RUBY#[D]storyteller} tales is my responsibility here in the tribe, and after so many years, it's time for me to come up with some originals.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And of course, something just had to go wrong with the Shadow Pin just as I was a few days into my musing... Because why would it ever rain when it could pour?

choices.text: So, will the rock fall down?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Now fair warning, that bit's just speculation. Things might not have gotten that bad yet...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But some accident has indeed happened with this Pin — one I can do nothing about.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is there really nothing you can do?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Well, I could make a record of it all, as an eyewitness. That way I'd also have a new tale, I guess.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Roawr...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you've just given up already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, there's something else Paimon wanted to ask. Why's the stone called a Shadow Pin? And what's this "shadow"?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *sigh* Were I telling the children a story, I'd say that the Wayob hung the Pins here to pin the shadow of the Volcano Lord in place...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But that which is sealed beneath them is, in truth, the Abyss.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's how most tales in Natlan are. They're embellished narratives held up as warnings, and all their rhetoric is a kind of metaphor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you mean the Abyss is actually sealed below here!?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's right. And two out of three small Shadow Pins have recently floated up. Perhaps when the third floats too, all the evil beneath the earth will come surging up like a tide.

choices.text: You have three of these!?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Three small and one large, actually, and this is the big one. The others look nothing like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, if the story's true, can't we just solve the problem by pushing the two pillars that have floated up back down?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *sigh* What an amazing idea — ah, if only you were the first to think of it.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: In fact, Lesser Shadow Pins have floated in the past, and according to the stories, that's exactly how it was handled. Things are trickier this time, though...

choices.text: ...Where the Abyss is involved, we can't stand idle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We've solved a whole bunch of similar problems before. We're experts now!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #Really? Not that I'm doubting your abilities — that much I could tell just from how you move, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I mean to say, are you really willing to help? Since it's the Abyss we're talking about, even I can't say for sure how dangerous things could get.

choices.text: Ooh, so scary. I regret everything. And alas! Now my stomach suddenly hurts...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hey, stop it! And Paimon just complimented you, too! Also, your acting is terrible!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, the point is that we'll help!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #See? {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]} agrees as well!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah, like a flame that appears in the darkness, so too will heroes rise up in times of great peril. Human possibility shines through in glory at moments such as this.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #You know what? This could make for a great story, too — indeed, {NICKNAME}, you've got some traits that even those storied heroes don't have. I'm looking forward to this, I must say.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Let's go, then, dear heroes. Let's go and check on our floating Shadow Pins.

choices.text: Oh dear, I do so fear, that danger's the only one for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we... No, that's not right! We've done a whole bunch of things that aren't dangerous too... Wait... Paimon's not sure what she's trying to say...

choices.text: Perhaps I could lend a hand?
Ooh, so there's still three more big stone pillars!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Friend... Don't mind me, but where does your interest in stone pillars come from? Also, let me remind you, the three Lesser Shadow Pins aren't anywhere near this large.

choices.text: "He saw the giant Shadow Pin plunge beneath the earth"...
Then what are you doing here?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I'm "caring" for this particular pillar.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}, are you all unhurt?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Paimon's okay, kinda.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rrooh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ah! You don't look injured, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}... Did the big pillar scare you just now?

choices.text: Good to see that you're okay.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rraaa... Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Back in action already? Hehe, you're awesome!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *cough* Well, that was a lucky break amidst our misfortune. This cloud of smoke is huge — every bit as large as the plumes of volcanic ash hurled out by the Volcano Lord in the stories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Paimon didn't think that the big Shadow Pin would come crashing down and bore such a big hole in the ground...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: As to that... *sigh* To be honest, I don't know what comes next.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But, uh, we can always inspect that hole first? For all we know, maybe this isn't too big a deal, right? It would be the right moment for some sort of ironic twist, after all!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: You know, like how a bandit finds that the treasure he's spent half his life searching for is actually worthless... Perhaps this place we've guarded for centuries has been empty all along...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Or maybe we'll find that the story of the Shadow Pins is but a five-centuries-old prank that some bored ancestor of ours came up with...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: ...Sorry, I know I'm rambling, but... I can't help but be nervous. Either way... I have no clue what we'll find down there.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But still... I... I will go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't worry about it, we'll come with you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It... doesn't look too serious. It's just a really big hole, right?

choices.text: Just the normal kind of big, really. The shape's kinda ugly, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When did you become some kinda "cavity connoisseur," huh? Sure, we've seen lots of these, but...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rraa, Rraa.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, don't you copy {M#him}{F#her} when {M#he's}{F#she's} being a bad role model! You don't want to pick up bad habits!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's where the Greater Shadow Pin fell, it seems. It's gone down much deeper than I imagined. It's almost like...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There was a huge open space down there to begin with...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Right. This huge space can't have appeared because the Shadow Pin fell through it. It must've been here long before, with the Shadow Pin suspended above it...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: ...To prevent anything that might crawl up from surfacing, perhaps?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rrooh...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Anyway, things look alright over here for now. I'll report this back to the tribe later...
Hsss... Argh! Ah—
Calamity— Pain— Save—

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Urgh... Wh—What was that...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hroo... Roar...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I heard a voice...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong? You all don't look so good — especially you, Titu...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: ...Heh, it's as I feared. The Iridescent Inscription on the Pin must've sensed something down there, causing it to fall.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That legend... is real... The spirits of the fallen Khaenri'ahn soldiers are about to emerge...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Roooawr.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Titu, are you okay?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Not really, I'm afraid. That voice... So cold, so coarse... Just listening to a few syllables was like running my brain across sandpaper...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, if it's that bad, why don't you stay here and keep watch? Just to make sure no one falls in and all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And as for us, we'll go down and see what's happening.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: No, you can't! It's dangerous down there. There's no reason you should be put in more peril, and I'll not be the one to do it...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've exchanged names, but not blows...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That makes us friends.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: ...Heh.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: So calm in the face of danger... Are you used to it, or is this just the natural result of possessing overwhelming strength?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: ...Well, let us go down together, then.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Though I do not have the power to resist the Abyss, as I am one who tells{RUBY#[D]storyteller} tales, I might be of some help regarding that below Natlan's surface.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Besides, to witness things to their completion is a storyteller's duty...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: ...But let's take five first. Once we're ready, let's head into this cavernous cavity, shall we?

choices.text: I'd only give this hole three stars...
*sniff* I was pretty frightened too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There, there, you two, don't be scared. The ever-reliable Paimon is here!

choices.text: There's no way I'd get injured with that much smoke around.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What does that even mean...

talks.objective: Go to the Lesser Shadow Pin with Titu

dialogues.text: Wow. Here I'd thought to come over and check on the frightening noises I'd heard...
Telling myself "Come on, Titu, it's probably nothing"... But this is quite something! Quite something indeed!

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!
There's even a little Tepetlisaurus here... Was it you who brought these outlanders here, then?
And... was it you who brought this Shadow Pin down?

choices.text: ...Should we not have done that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eh? Wait, did we do something bad, {NICKNAME}? If we act fast, while there's only one witness...
#Haha, come on, no need for that! It's not serious, and if anything, I'd say you've done us a favor! So, you're {NICKNAME}, then? Who's your friend over there?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #And this is {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.
And Titu's my name, a teller {RUBY#[D]storyteller}of tales for our tribe. I'm also responsible for "caring" for the stone pillars in this valley.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And of course, this Shadow Pin you've plunged into the earth is one of three little pins, and its care is within my jurisdiction.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: J—Jurisdiction... Uh oh, looks like we're going to have to compensate the locals for dropping that stone pillar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon wouldn't have used our real name's if she'd known sooner.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Compensate... "Titu had a flash of inspiration. Perhaps he might use this to coerce these people into helping him achieve his goals..."

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's how I'd slot a bit like this into the plot, anyway.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah, sorry, got a bit carried away thinking about stories there. Telling{RUBY#[D]storyteller} tales is my responsibility here in the tribe, and after so many years, it's time for me to come up with some originals.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And of course, something just had to go wrong with the Shadow Pin just as I was a few days into my musing... Because why would it ever rain when it could pour?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ahem! Anyway, I'm not gonna blackmail you. I—I mean, I wouldn't have spoken my thoughts aloud if that was the case, right?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Look, we exchanged names, but we haven't come to blows, so that makes us friends, yes?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: In that case... could you listen to a friend's request?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure... as long as it doesn't involve compensation.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: No, no, surely not! Hmm, how should I put this? ... When you passed through the valley, did you see some sort of giant block of solid phlogiston with golden patterns carved into it?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: It's in the center of this place. You can't miss it.

choices.text: That rings a bell...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: This whole business I'm talking about has to do with that huge stone pillar. We call it a Shadow Pin... and we've had problems with it recently.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: To be honest, I'd all but given up before meeting you. I had the line all ready: "The Shadow Pins could not be saved, dooming the tribe to calamitous destruction"... It didn't sound too bad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, it's just a stone pillar. How could it destroy the tribe?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, what's so special about these "Shadow Pins" anyway? And the one we dropped, it was a... lesser pin? But it seemed pretty big to Paimon, so why's it called that?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Hmm... Since you're both outlanders, I suppose a more detailed explanation is in order. This is related to a legend handed down through our tribe.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: The stories say that the Wayob hung the Pins here to seal the shadow of the Volcano Lord...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But that which is sealed beneath them is, in truth, the Abyss.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's how most tales in Natlan are. They're embellished narratives held up as warnings, and all their rhetoric is a kind of metaphor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you mean the Abyss is actually sealed below here!?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's right. And recently, two out of the three little Shadow Pins have floated upward. Perhaps if the third floats too, all the evil beneath the earth will come surging up like a tide.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: So to be honest, it's an unexpected boon that you've managed to push one back in. So, no compensation required.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: If anything, I was hoping to ask if you'd mind pushing the other one back in as well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh... What do you think, {NICKNAME}...?

choices.text: ...Where the Abyss is involved, we can't stand idle.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Even you're up for it, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}? Well, alright then.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah, like a flame that appears in the darkness, so too will heroes rise up in times of great peril. Human possibility shines through in glory at moments such as this.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #You know what? This could make for a great story, too — indeed, {NICKNAME}, you've got some traits that even those storied heroes don't have. I'm looking forward to this, I must say.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Let's go, then, dear heroes. Let's go and check on the last floating Pin...

choices.text: Perhaps I could lend a hand?
Nope, don't recall anything like that...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Huh. I thought it was obvious enough. That's fine, though.

choices.text: Paimon did it. I was just walking over here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! You're always like that! Paimon'll get mad if you don't cut it out!
#Haha, relax. If anything, this is a huge relief. So your name's Paimon, then? In that case, how about this {M#good fellow}{F#good lady} over here?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Call me {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: I can't believe that worked. That was truly a scene from out of story and song.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #See, Paimon told you {NICKNAME}'s super strong!

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe, you think so, don'cha, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: #You weren't affected by the Abyss, were you, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Relax, it's just the Abyss...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #Even our strongest warriors must remain vigilant and then some in the face of the Abyss. You're no ordinary person, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Haha, who knows, the story I spin from this material might even surpass those by Sanhaj!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Ehrrr?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this Sanhaj some sort of big deal?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Haha, for "those who tell stories in their tribes," Sanhaj of the Masters of the Night-Wind is worthy of reverence indeed...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: They say he had every scroll ever written up to his time committed to memory, and that he was willing to go from tribe to tribe and share those tales... That said, they also say that he also mooched a lot of food and drink off of them along the way...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Stories speak of bygone times, but they also represent the wisdom of our forebears. Thus, the mere act of sharing it was seen as a selfless act, so all both loved and hated cunning Sanhaj.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Later, that tale-telling hero would himself become part of a heroic tale — a fate I doubt even he ever envisioned... But yeah. Sanhaj was an amazing storyteller.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's the story...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #That's right. All the characters in Sanhaj's tales were some kind of tribal warriors and dragons, though. In mine, we'll have you, {NICKNAME}, and Paimon...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: So, if only in terms of the variety of the main cast, I'm the winner!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Don't forget to include {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah yes, of course, of course. Storytellers never forget a single character!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Alright then. Let's head for the next floating Shadow Pin. I want to fix this issue and start writing by nightfall!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo! Let's go, let's go!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

choices.text: I'm alright for now.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: These days, none understand the meaning hidden in these lights. Only the golden engravings, scattered across Natlan, remain to mark the trail of those ancient dragons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you know how to work it, but not how it works?

dialogues.text: So, Liyue has those mysterious adeptal mechanisms, yes? And while humans don't know the principles underlying their function, they can still make use of them.

response.speaker: Paimon

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now, at the previous stone pillars, we also let the golden pattern fly under said pillars first...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Yes, that is indeed the correct sealing process.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #Anyway, if you're ready, {NICKNAME}, please touch the inscription beneath the Pin. We've got to collect as much of the inscription's power — scattered as it is around the stone pillars — as we can.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Of course, the Abyss will resist, so... please be careful.

choices.text: Is your stomach upset?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hrrr?

response.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: W—We did it... The two Shadow Pins have been plunged back into the earth.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice work!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Another round of applause couldn't hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: I'd clap my hands 'till they fell off if I could — but then I couldn't write another story, so forgive me for not doing so.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Still, I assure you that in my heart, naught but bones remain attached to my wrists.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Roawr...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, yeah. That's getting kinda creepy.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Really? Hmm, and here I thought that kids these days like their stories with a little dash of darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Ah, watching the Shadow Pin burrow back into the ground really takes a load off my soul.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Long-standing tradition dictates that we now only need to check the third Lesser Shadow Pin and the Greater Shadow Pin, and we can call this a job well done. Abyss successfully busted, not to return for a good long time.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: The rest of this trip should be quite safe, so feel free to come along and chat with me! I'd like to know the heroes I'm inscribing into our tribe's stories better, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! In that case, you've gotta say something like this: "The mighty Paimon was as tall as a mountain..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In that case, I'd like to be as large as two.

dialogues.text: Rawr, rawr, rawr!

choices.text: #Ah, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}, you truly are a Saurian of prodigious appetites...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: There we go! That's the second Lesser Shadow Pin!

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: The seals around this Pin have been damaged far more than the first... Even the Iridescent Inscription has been pushed outside the pillar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that what's you call that shiny, golden thing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now that you mention it, I think we've seen them before...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: That's right. There should have been something similar on the Pin you pushed back into the ground earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Ancient legends tell that before the idea of Natlan was even born, when this land was ruled by the ancient dragons, the language by which they wielded phlogiston was these Iridescent Inscriptions.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: These days, none understand the meaning hidden in these lights. Only the golden engravings, scattered across Natlan, remain to mark the trail of those ancient dragons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you know how to work it, but not how it works?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: We cannot decipher the meaning of the inscriptions, but the ways we use phlogiston are the same, so we do understand it on that level. Let me try to explain...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: So, Liyue has those mysterious adeptal mechanisms, yes? And while humans don't know the principles underlying their function, they can still make use of them.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: That's more or less what I'm talking about, despite the imperfect analogy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So much to say that we'll need this shiny Iridescent Inscription to push the Pin back down, right?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Correct. Think of the Inscription as an eggshell that has been shattered by the expanding Abyss. We'll need to find the broken shards and fix the shell — only then can the Abyss within be sealed away...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Huh. That's a better analogy than the last.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks so too! Now she gets it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, the golden patterns flew right over, just like before, but the Inscription hasn't appeared beneath this pillar... Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: That indicates that not only has the Inscription been squeezed out, but it's also become fragmented... This is bad. We need to find any scattered bits, and fast.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, where do we find them?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: ...I don't know either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: They should still be held down by some power despite being scattered, so my guess is that they're nearby. Maybe we just need to look around...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr, rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? You wanna go over? We're doing something important right now — we'll play with you later, alright?

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Mrrraa... Rawr! Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you mean that the Inscription is over there?

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Oh wow! I've heard that even now, there are still Saurians who can sense an Inscription's power, but I always thought it was hearsay — could it be true?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: #I suppose you really are no ordinary Tepetlisaurus, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you can do that too, huh? ...Hmph! You've got some way to go before you can be as good a guide as Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Ehrrr?

choices.text: Paimon's jealous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Says who? Paimon's way more broad-minded than she looks! That was just her way of praising him!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Err... Err?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* The little guy didn't catch that at all. Bah, if only he was a little smarter...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm sure he'll understand someday...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Precisely. Those in the tribe responsible for Saurian care always say that it takes time to truly establish a rapport with them.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: The secret to success is as follows — exercise patience, and constantly communicate. Whether humans wish to understand Saurians, or Saurians humans, they both need... lots and lots of time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #True... Just like Paimon didn't get what {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]} was trying to tell us just now either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Sorry, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rrraa, Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're quick to reply though, Paimon'll give you that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, we'll follow you and see if we can find any golden patterns.

choices.text: See, Paimon's praising you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's true, but don't let it go to your head now...

talks.objective: Head to the last Lesser Shadow Pin

dialogues.text: ...This is a big problem. Man, haha, what terrible luck! Still, wouldn't this make for a pretty interesting story opener?

"Titu, the tribe's old storyteller, spoke of what he had seen: On the day of that great earthquake, he saw the giant Shadow Pin plunge beneath the earth — and that was how all the calamities began..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa. This person sure is spouting some scary stuff.
Ah, yes. "You've sure gotten slow. Didn't even notice them until they were right under your nose." That line's from a story I read recently. Made a real impression on me.
Still, if you ask me, eavesdropping isn't usually considered a sign of virtue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't blame us, you were the one talking super loudly.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!
Really? Well, that makes things awkward... And hey! C'mon, little fella, why are you backing these outlanders? Just whose side are you on?

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr... Rawrr!
Alright, alright... Still, it's quite the strange little ensemble. Two outlanders and a special little Tepetlisaurus. That social studies bookworm sure would love to see this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wait, you can understand what {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}'s saying?
#Understand Saurian-speak? Haha, you've got to be kidding me. No one can do that! What do you think they'd say anyway? "Hello, my name is {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}"?

But I'm one of the Children of Echoes, and we're always around Tepetlisaurs. You can figure out what they're trying to communicate from their eyes, their expressions, and the humming noises they make.
Anyway, introductions are in order. Titu... That's my name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #And this is {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Haha, alright then. Here in Natlan, those who exchange names but not blows are considered friends — and friends we shall be!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Titu, you say... Oh, so you're Titu! We met a sentry on our way here named Yukom, who wanted you to get back to your post!

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Oh, so he was the one taking the shift before mine... *sigh* Unfortunately, he'll have to wait a little longer. I feel for him, but I've got something more important to take care of right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And what's that important matter? Standing around?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Ah, you don't understand, little outlander Paimon. This is a critical yet boring place — though it is filled with naught but stone pillars, my presence alone is itself key.

choices.text: Whoa, now those are big stone pillars!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Uh, that's... not the response I expected. In fact, that's a worrying amount of excitement about... *sigh* big stone pillars...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: It's been doing poorly of late, I'm afraid. "The Shadow Pin's spirit was weakening, and the shadow it should have pinned in place would soon silently slip away..."

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Hmm. You know what? That would make a good starting point for a story.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Ehrrr?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah, sorry, got a bit carried away thinking about stories there. Telling{RUBY#[D]storyteller} tales is my responsibility here in the tribe, and after so many years, it's time for me to come up with some originals.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And of course, something just had to go wrong with the Shadow Pin just as I was a few days into my musing... Because why would it ever rain when it could pour?

choices.text: So, will this rock fall down?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Now fair warning, that bit's just speculation. Things might not have gotten that bad yet.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But some accident has indeed happened with this Pin — one I can do nothing about.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is there really nothing you can do?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Well, I could make a record of it all, as an eyewitness. That way I'd also have a new tale, I guess.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Roawr...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you've just given up already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, there's something else Paimon wanted to ask. Why's this called a Shadow Pin? And what's this "shadow"?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *sigh* Were I telling the children a story, I'd say that the Wayob hung the Pins here to pin the shadow of the Volcano Lord in place...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But that which is sealed beneath them is, in truth, the Abyss.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's how most tales in Natlan are. They're embellished narratives held up as warnings, and all their rhetoric is a kind of metaphor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you mean the Abyss is actually sealed below here!?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's right. And two out of three small Shadow Pins have recently floated up. Perhaps when the third floats too, all the evil beneath the earth will come surging up like a tide.

choices.text: You have three of these!?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Three small and one large, actually, and this is the big one. The others look nothing like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, if the story's true, can't we just solve the problem by pushing the two pillars that have floated up back down?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *sigh* What an amazing idea — ah, if only you were the first to think of it.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: In fact, Lesser Shadow Pins have floated in the past, and according to the stories, that's exactly how it was handled. Things are trickier this time, though...

choices.text: ...Where the Abyss is involved, we can't stand idle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We've solved a whole bunch of similar problems before. We're experts now!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #Really? Not that I'm doubting your abilities — that much I could tell just from how you move, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I mean to say, are you really willing to help? Since it's the Abyss we're talking about, even I can't say for sure how dangerous things could get.

choices.text: Ooh, so scary. I regret everything. And alas! Now my stomach suddenly hurts...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hey, stop it! And Paimon just complimented you, too! Also, your acting is terrible!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, the point is that we'll help!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #See? {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]} agrees as well!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah, like a flame that appears in the darkness, so too will heroes rise up in times of great peril. Human possibility shines through in glory at moments such as this.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #You know what? This could make for a great story, too — indeed, {NICKNAME}, you've got some traits that even those storied heroes don't have. I'm looking forward to this, I must say.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Let's go, then, dear heroes. Let's go and check on our floating Shadow Pins.

choices.text: Oh dear, I do so fear, that danger's the only one for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we... No, that's not right! We've done a whole bunch of things that aren't dangerous too... Wait... Paimon's not sure what she's trying to say...

choices.text: Perhaps I could lend a hand.
Ooh, so there's still three more big stone pillars!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Friend... Don't mind me, but where does your interest in stone pillars come from? Also, let me remind you, the three Lesser Shadow Pins aren't anywhere near this large.

choices.text: "He saw the giant Shadow Pin plunge beneath the earth"...
Then what are you doing here?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I'm "caring" for this particular pillar.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Wonderful, it's solid — almost as if it was grown from the very soil, more robust even than the roots of the great mother-tree that grows beneath the Scions of the Canopy's mountain cliffs... Now I can head back and take up my shift in peace.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Of the three Lesser Shadow Pins, the most reliable you remained. If I should ever pen a tale about the Pins transforming into lovely tribeswomen, you shall be loveliest amongst them.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Errr?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so you were the one most interested in stone pillars all along, huh? Shocking.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Hey, now, that's ignorance speaking. Here in Natlan, we believe that pure spirit and intelligence dwell within all things... For us, "things taking on human form" is a most traditional theme.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: For example, the tale of a beach tree's shadow that transformed into a young woman and a young Flower-Feather Clan tribesman who fell from the sky... Or the story of a man who was human by day, but would morph into a Saurian under the moonlight at night.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Many are the ways such tales are told, but they're all variations on that same theme I spoke of.

choices.text: Is that really true?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *cough* Well, that is what a lot of stories say — that much, I'll swear to as one who tells{RUBY#[D]storyteller} tales.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what about the Shadow Pin story, then? There's no real shadow of the Volcano Lord, is there? And if the shadow is the Abyss, then what is a Pin, really?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: ...Oh ho, you're a lot sharper than I thought, little Paimon.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Let's see. Where should I start with such a "story"... Long ago, the mountain range where the Children of Echoes made their home was not as it is today... It was more normal, more complete, more lovely.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Everything changed... when the Khaenri'ahn catastrophe struck.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Khaenri'ahn catastrophe?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Indeed. Natlan's Ley Lines were always special and somewhat delicate... and so this calamity brought utter devastation.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: They say that the Night Kingdom was severely damaged in that disaster, and the totem poles' lights grew dim. The Wayob could not hear the tribes' cries...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And up on land, a dark tide of disaster blazed toward the mountain range, brought on by two Khaenri'ahn soldiers — it was they who were the source of the troubles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Khaenri'ahn soldiers?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's right. At that time, the tribe's leader had gone forth to the lone island in the west to resist the giant beasts. Elder Traore had no choice but to contend with the Abyss... and those two abject Khaenri'ahns.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Finally, the tribes' warriors and Saurians, exhausting their spirit, flesh, and blood, found a way to use the Iridescent Inscription, fashioning giant stone nails out of solid phlogiston...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And Elder Traore was first to leap into the dark pit, crying, "If the Abyss should ensnare death, let us flip the script! With death and sacrifice, we shall ensnare the Abyss!"

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: The brave warriors followed him in, and after much sacrifice, the Abyss was, at last, sealed beneath the earth.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: This is the true tale of the past. Even the Children of Echoes, who excavate solid phlogiston and gems for a living, know that the phlogiston around the stone nails must remain untouched.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's the story...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rroo...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That happened five centuries ago... And yet you made it sound like it was something you saw yourself!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's a storyteller's duty. I love my work... And amongst all the tales I tell, I love the stories of these heroes the most.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I'm not a nimble fellow, nor am I the best fighter. If anything, I'm the furthest thing from a hero.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But when I tell their stories, I feel like I'm right there, traveling, adventuring, and fighting alongside them...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I feel them smile upon me, egging me on, as if standing in the shadows of the bonfires, listening to me as they would a friend bragging of their exploits.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And perhaps that is how I fight alongside them, by ensuring that their stories will be passed down and remembered, from generation to generation.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Hmmm. Wait a second. So what does that elder's story have to do with the Volcano Lord, and why do Shadow Pins have that name?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Hahaha, still thinking about that, Paimon?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: It's simple. It's just a little play on words, commonly done in many stories...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: It's called a Shadow Pin... because it pins shadows. Easy, right?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Urgh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Urgh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wow, the two of you made the same noise...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not where Paimon thought this was going...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait, what's going on? You're shaking up and down, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's the ground that's shaking, Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I blame Titu's awful jape...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on! My joke wasn't that disastrous!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: It's the big Shadow Pin. That's where the tremors are coming from.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Something's wrong. Come on. We need to get back there...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Why did this... We drove all three Lesser Pins into the ground, but the Abyss's influence is getting stronger...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's impossible. The woven scrolls' stories clearly state that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Things our experiences do not prepare us for do sometimes happen...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's more accurate to say that accidents happen so often that even Paimon's stopped being surprised...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Could it be that... some change has overtaken the Abyss surging within the Ley Lines, causing its resistance to grow stronger...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Either way, it feels like something terrible's happening down there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't we try getting a closer look?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #P—Please do, {NICKNAME}...

choices.text: Sounds a little dubious to me...

talks.objective: Investigate the area beneath the canyon

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: #What's wrong, {NICKNAME}? Just touch the Iridescent Inscription beneath the Lesser Shadow Pin if you want to start gathering the inscription's power.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Be sure to stay safe, though...
Well now, and here I'd thought to come over and check on the frightening noises I'd heard...
Telling myself "Come on, Titu, it's probably nothing"... But this is quite something! Quite something indeed!

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!
There's even a little Tepetlisaurus here... Was it you who brought these outlanders here, then?
And... was it you who brought this Shadow Pin down?

choices.text: ...Should we not have done that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eh? Wait, did we do something bad, {NICKNAME}? If we act fast, while there's only one witness...
#Haha, come on, no need for that! It's not serious, and if anything, I'd say you've done us a favor! So, you're {NICKNAME}, then? Who's your friend over there?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #And this is {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.
And Titu's my name, a teller {RUBY#[D]storyteller}of tales for our tribe. I'm also responsible for "caring" for the stone pillars in this valley.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you're Titu! We met a sentry on our way here named Yukom, who wanted you to get back to your post!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Oh, so he was the one taking the shift before mine... *sigh* Unfortunately, he'll have to wait a little longer. I feel for him, but I've got something more important to take care of right now.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: These pillars, also named Shadow Pins, are under my jurisdiction, and I must take care of them before things take a turn for the worse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: J—Jurisdiction... Uh oh, looks like we're going to have to compensate the locals for dropping that stone pillar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon wouldn't have used our real name's if she'd known sooner.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Compensate... "Titu had a flash of inspiration. Perhaps he might use this to coerce these people into helping him achieve his goals..."

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's how I'd slot a bit like this into the plot, anyway.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah, sorry, got a bit carried away thinking about stories there. I've been telling them in our tribe for so many years, and now it's finally reached the point that I need to come up with some originals.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And of course, something just had to go wrong with the Shadow Pin just as I was a few days into my musing... Because why would it ever rain when it could pour?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ahem! Anyway, I'm not gonna blackmail you. I—I mean, I wouldn't have spoken my thoughts aloud if that was the case, right?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Look, we exchanged names, but we haven't come to blows, so that makes us friends, yes?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: In that case... could you listen to a friend's request?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure... as long as it doesn't involve compensation.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: No, no, surely not! Hmm, how should I put this? ... When you passed through the valley, did you see some sort of giant block of solid phlogiston with golden patterns carved into it?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: It's in the center of this place. You can't miss it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nope, don't recall anything like that...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Huh. I thought it was obvious enough. That's fine, though.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: This whole business I'm talking about has to do with that huge stone pillar. We call it a Shadow Pin... and we've had problems with it recently.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: To be honest, I'd all but given up before meeting you. "Let's just have the stone pillar problem cause the tribe's destruction. That story would work too, right?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, it's just a stone pillar. How could it destroy the whole tribe? That seems kinda ridiculous...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, what's so special about these "Shadow Pins" anyway? And the one we dropped, it was a... lesser pin? But it seemed pretty big to Paimon, so why's it called that?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Hmm... Since you're both outlanders, I suppose a more detailed explanation is in order. This is related to a legend handed down through our tribe.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: The stories say that the Wayob hung the Pins here to seal the shadow of the Volcano Lord...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But that which is sealed beneath them is, in truth, the Abyss.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's how most tales in Natlan are. They're embellished narratives held up as warnings, and all their rhetoric is a kind of metaphor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you mean the Abyss is actually sealed below here!?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: That's right. And recently, two out of the three little Shadow Pins have floated upward. Perhaps if the third floats too, all the evil beneath the earth will come surging up like a tide.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: So to be honest, it's an unexpected boon that you've managed to push one back in. So, no compensation required.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: If anything, I was hoping to ask if you'd mind pushing the other one back in as well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh... What do you think, {NICKNAME}...?

choices.text: ...Where the Abyss is involved, we can't stand idle.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Even you're up for it, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}? Well, alright then.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Ah, like a flame that appears in the darkness, so too will heroes rise up in times of great peril. Human possibility shines through in glory at moments such as this.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #You know what? This could make for a great story, too — indeed, {NICKNAME}, you've got some traits that even those storied heroes don't have. I'm looking forward to this, I must say.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Let's go, then, dear heroes. Let's go and check on the last floating Lesser Pin...

choices.text: Perhaps I could lend a hand?
Paimon did it. I was just walking over here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! You're always like that! Paimon'll get mad if you don't cut it out!
#Haha, relax. If anything, this is a huge relief. So your name's Paimon, then? In that case, how about this {M#good fellow}{F#good lady} over here?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Call me {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: There we go! That's the second Lesser Shadow Pin!

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: But if memory serves, the seals around this second one should be far more badly damaged than the ones on the first...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Did things change for the better, or was there some kind soul who...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, the kind souls you're talking about are right here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right. We found the Iridescent Inscription earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was split into two parts, and hidden real deep to boot!

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Haha, is that so... To think that the toughest of the Pins to fix was... Ah! Surely, a star of good fortune shines upon me this day—

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: —That I was able to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Either way, no time to lose! Let's head under the Shadow Pin and have a look at things!

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Ancient legends tell that before the idea of Natlan was even born, when this land was ruled by the ancient dragons, the language by which they wielded phlogiston was these Iridescent Inscriptions.

dialogues.speaker: Yukom
dialogues.text: *sigh* How did it go? Did you find Titu?

dialogues.speaker: Yukom
dialogues.text: Ugh, that guy... He's a good storyteller, I'll give him that — but he's just no good as a guard.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Shadow Pins, hmmm... Shadow Pins...
